scope: Read model.py/model.json and independently compare all concrete scenario memberships and event sets with required 2-partition example and KafkaConsumer source group semantics. Not a second execution of implementation verifier, and not a Kafka runtime experiment.
sourceLocations: sources/KafkaConsumer.java:96-123 (group.id, exclusive per-group partition assignment, logical subscriber)
sources/design.md:137-157 (consumer fetch positions and per-group partition ownership)
sources/design.md:248-255 (Share Groups are a distinct model)
conclusions: Wrong shared group gives notification E01/E03 and points E02/E04; each misses two required events.
Separate groups each get all four identities from the same retained P0/P1 logs; display sequence across partitions is not a total-order guarantee.
Notify expands to N1 owning P0 and N2 owning P1; points remains one member reading both partitions.
All examples explicitly use fresh groups without commits, earliest and retained beginning 0. Results do not promise all history for every new group.
Teaching scenario resets before third comparison avoid claiming membership change rewinds a live consumer group.
limitations: No broker/client, live rebalance, business side effect, fault recovery or exactly-once execution validated.
